newsitem.title: USA: Clinton approves U.S. sanctions against Burma.
newsitem.headline: Clinton approves U.S. sanctions against Burma.

text.p: President Bill Clinton has approved imposing economic sanctions against Burma due to human rights abuses by the Burmese military government, a Clinton administration official said early on Tuesday.
The State Department would announce the sanctions, which will involve banning new U.S. investment in Burma, later on Tuesday, the official told Reuters.

The official said Clinton made the decision within the last few days since Burma's military government had become "increasingly repressive lately" and was ignoring international calls for progress toward a democratically elected government.

The United States and many other Western countries have criticized Burma for human rights abuses and for failing to recognize the democratically elected government of the National League for Democracy, which was co-founded by Aung San Suu Kyi.

Suu Kyi was under house arrest for six years for her criticism of the Rangoon government. Clinton can impose sanctions on Burma if the democracy leader is arrested again or the situation in Burma worsens.
Last week, Secretary of State Madeleine Albright, who is expected to announce the ban on Tuesday, criticized Burma's military government for failing to respond to appeals to improve human rights.
